questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A1=5

x2=52[sin2πt+cos2πt]

x2=10sin2πT+π4

questions.q: A block of mass 2 kg is attached with two identical springs of spring constant 20 N m-1 each. The block is placed on a frictionless surface and the ends of the springs are attached to rigid supports (see figure). When the mass is displaced from its equilibrium position, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The time period of oscillation is πX in SI unit. The value of X is______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the block is displaced by a distance x, force acting on block due to both springs will be in the same direction. Therefore,

F=-2kx⇒a=-2kmx,

Comparing it witha=-ω2x , we get

ω=2km=2×202

=20 rad s-1

Now, T=2πω=2π20=π5

Hence, required value of X=5.

questions.q: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>_________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The total energy of the harmonic oscillator is given by the formula

E=12kA2   ...1

where, k is the force constant and A is the amplitude.

The potential energy of the oscillator at the given displacement can be written as

U=12kA32=kA22×9=E9

Hence, its kinetic energy is given by

KE=E-E9=8E9

Thus, the required ratio is

EKE=E8E9=98

Hence, x=9.

questions.q: The time period of simple harmonic motion of mass M in the given figure is παM5K, where the value of α is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For series combination of the spring, equivalent spring constant is given by, 1keq=1k1+1k2.

Therefore, for combined system net spring constant keq=2k×k2k+k+k=5k3

Angular frequency of oscillation ω=keqm

⇒ω=5k3m

Period of oscillation τ=2πω=2π3m5k

=π12m5k

Therefore, α=12.

questions.q: Two waves executing simple harmonic motion travelling in the same direction with same amplitude and frequency are superimposed. The resultant amplitude is equal to the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math> times of amplitude of individual motions. The phase difference between the two motions is _____ (degree)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When two waves of the same frequency superimpose, the resultant amplitude is given by

Aresultant =A12+A22+2A1A2cosϕ

⇒3 A=A2+A2+2A2cosϕ

⇒3A2=2A2+2A2cosϕ

⇒cosϕ=12

∴ϕ=60°

∴Phase difference =60 degree

questions.q: A simple pendulum with length 100 cm and bob of mass 250 g is executing S.H.M of amplitude 10 cm. The maximum tension in the string is found to be x40 N. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the given figure we can see that 

sinθ0=Al=10100=110

From conservation of energy mv22=mgl(1-cosθ0)

Maximum tension occurs at mean position

T=mg+mv2l⇒T=mg+2mg(1-cosθ0)

Substituting the values,

T=mg(1+2(1-1-sin2θ0)⇒T=mg(3-21-1100)⇒T=0.25×9.8(3-2(1-1200))⇒T=0.25×9.8×1.01=2.4745 N

It is given that

 T=x40⇒x=40×2.4745=98.98≈99

questions.q: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, attached to a horizontal spring, executes SHM with an amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. When this mass passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>124</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is placed over it and both masses move together with amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. If the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At mean position, the velocity of the particle in S.H.M. is maximum, so kinetic energy is KE=12kA2, where, k is spring constant.

We also know that, kinetic energy is related to momentum as KE=p22m.

Now, from both equations, we have 

12kA2=p22m     (Here, momentum is conserved)

⇒A1 A22=m2 m1=1024900

⇒A1 A2=3230=1615=1616-1

∴α=16

questions.q: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The frequency of oscillations if a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mi>m</mi></math> is suspended from the same spring is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of oscillation of a spring-block system is given by, f=12πkm

Therefore, for both cases, we can write

f1=12πkm and 

f2=12πk9m

Required ratio, f1f2=91=31

questions.q:
Two simple harmonic motion, are represented by the equations

y1=10sin3πt+π3;  y2=5(sin3πt+3cos3πt)

Ratio of amplitude of y1 to y2=x:1. The value of x is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
y1=10sin3πt+π3

y2=5[sin3πt+3cosπt]

y2=10sin3πt+π3⇒A2 A1=1010=1

questions.q: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></math>. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> be its time period. The slope of its potential energy (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>U</mi></math>) – time (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math>) curve will be maximum when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>T</mi><mi>β</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, displacement x=A sin ωt

Now, potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is U=12mω2x2=12mω2A2sin2ωt,

So, slope of potential energy and time curve is dUdt=12mω3A22sin2ωt

Now, dUdtmax will be maximum when sin2ωt=1

 ⇒2ωt=π2⇒22πTt=π2⇒t=T8⇒β=8

questions.q: As per given figures, two springs of spring constants K and 2 K are connected to mass m. If the period of oscillation in figure (a) is 3 s, then the period of oscillation in figure (b) will be x s. The value of x is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In figure (a), the springs are connected in series. Therefore,

Keq=K1K2K1+K2=K×2KK+2K=2K3

Therefore, the time period

Ta=2πmKeq=2πm2K3=2π3m2K

In figure (b), the springs are connected in parallel. Therefore,

Keq=K1+K2=3K

Therefore, the time period

Tb=2πmKeq=2πm3K

Now,

TaTb=92⇒Tb=23Ta=2 s

Hence, x=2

questions.q: A pendulum bob has a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at its lowest position. The pendulum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long. The speed of bob, when the length makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> to the vertical will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying work energy theorem:

wg+wT=ΔK

-mgl1-cos60°=12mv2-12mu2

v2=u2-2gl1-cos60°

v2=9-2×10×0.512

v2=4

v=2 m s-1

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>α</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo></math>______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at the mean position is given by

V=Aω   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

10=4×ω⇒ω=52 rad s-1

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at any instantaneous position x can be expressed as

v=ωA2-x2   ...2

From equation (2), it follows that

5=5242-x2⇒x2=16-4=12⇒x=12 cm

Hence, α=12.

questions.q: A rectangular block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> attached to a horizontal spiral spring executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and time period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The maximum force exerted by spring on block is ___ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By Newton's second law,

F=mamax.

The maximum acceleration for a SHM is given by 

amax=ω2A   ...(i)

The time period is given by 

T=2πω=3.14 s

⇒ω=2πT=2π3.14=2 rad s-1

Thus, the maximum acceleration from equation (i)

amax=4×1=4 m s-2

The maximum force is 

F=5 kg×4 m s-2=20 N

questions.q: The amplitude of a particle executing SHM is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The displacement at which its kinetic energy will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></math> more than the potential energy is: ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let x be the displacement at which its kinetic energy will be 25% more than the potential energy.

Given here, A=3 cm and KE=PE+PE4

So, KE=54PE

⇒12mω2A2-x2=54×12mω2x2

⇒A2-x2=54x2

⇒9x24=A2

⇒x=23A

∴ x=23×3 cm

⇒x=2 cm

questions.q:
A particle of mass $0.50 \mathrm{~kg}$ executes simple harmonic motion under force $F=-50\left(\mathrm{Nm}^{-1}\right) x$. The time period of oscillation is $\frac{x}{35} \mathrm{~s}$. The value of $x$ is _______
(Given $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{~F}=-50(\mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{ma}=(-50 \mathrm{x}) \\ & 0.5 \mathrm{a}=-50 \mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{a}=(-100 \mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{W}^2=100 \Rightarrow(\mathrm{w}=10) \\ & \mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi}{10}=\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)=\frac{22}{7 \times 15}=\left(\frac{22}{35}\right) \\ & \frac{\pi}{35}=\frac{22}{35} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=22\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The velocity of a particle executing SHM varies with displacement (x) as 4v2=50–x2. The time period of oscillations is x7 s. The value of x is ______.

[Take π=227]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

4v2=50-x2

⇒v=1250-x2

Comparing with standard equation of SHM, v=ωA2-x2, we get

ω=12

Now,

T=2πω=4π=887

Hence, required x=88.

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and time period is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The time it will take to travel from its position of maximum displacement to the point corresponding to half of its amplitude, is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, A=8 cm and T=6 s

The displacement equation in SHM, when amplitude is halved is Acos2πtT=A2

⇒2πtT=π3

Time taken by the particle is t= T6=66=1sec.
